task: Known-order continuous angle-delay-Doppler recovery from a dense noisy third-order tensor

dataset.split: evaluation-only baseline verification; no parameter tuning on pilot truth

source.mechanism_reference: Mamandipoor, Ramasamy, and Madhow, Newtonized Orthogonal Matching Pursuit: Frequency Estimation Over the Continuum, IEEE TSP 2016, DOI 10.1109/TSP.2016.2580523
source.isac_reference: Shah et al., Newtonized Orthogonal Matching Pursuit for High-Resolution Target Detection in Sparse OFDM ISAC Systems, arXiv:2411.03191 / IEEE TVT DOI 10.1109/TVT.2025.3573165

known_deviations: The reference ISAC method is two-dimensional delay-Doppler recovery on sparse OFDM resources; this baseline extends the mechanism to a dense three-dimensional tensor.
The pilot uses known target count for an equal support budget instead of CFAR termination.

The implementation uses residual-domain local oversampling, safeguarded per-atom Newton steps, cyclic feedback, and joint LS, not the reference paper's full block-Hessian sparse-resource implementation.
Therefore manuscript text must use '3-D cyclic NOMP-inspired comparator', not 'reproduced NOMP-OFDM-ISAC'.
